items.q: Do I need to be a business major or have consulting experience?
items.a: No. SCG is open to all undergraduates at the University of Maryland who are in good academic standing and meet the semester requirement. Our projects need data science, engineering, design, research and communication skills as much as business skills, and we teach consulting methods in onboarding.

items.q: I'm a CS, engineering or data science student. What would I actually do?
items.a: [TBD: officers to confirm.] Examples from recent projects: building and benchmarking forecasting models, configuring a SQL database and dashboards, and documenting systems and processes. See the Projects page for what each team did.
All academically eligible students at the University of Maryland with five or more semesters before graduation may be considered. This includes semesters from a Plus-1, MS/A, or MBA program.

items.q: If I've applied once, can I apply again?
items.a: Absolutely. We encourage previous applicants to reapply if they are still interested and eligible.

items.q: Does it cost money to join?
items.a: No. SCG is 100% free to join. We are funded by the generous support of the Ed Snider Center for Enterprise and Markets and our alumni.

items.q: What makes SCG different from other on-campus consulting groups?
items.a: SCG's clients are on-campus organizations, so members make lasting changes in the UMD community they are part of. SCG also partners with EY, whose consultants guide every client team.
items.note: Edited: the old answer's ranking claim (Vault, 2021) was dropped as unverifiable and dated.

items.q: How many people do you accept each semester?
items.a: There is no predetermined number of analyst positions in any semester. SCG is an intentionally small and close-knit community, so we weigh the size of the applicant pool and our graduating seniors, and we look at each candidate's accomplishments and overall fit.

items.q: What does the interview look like?
items.a: There are two rounds. The first is a team interview where you work through a case in a group. The final round is 60 minutes: 30 minutes of behavioral questions and 30 minutes of case. Our interview prep page has sample behavioral questions, a case framework guide and practice cases.

items.q: What is life like for members?
items.a: Consultants attend weekly general body meetings or workshops, weekly team project meetings, and occasional social outings.

New analysts take part in faculty and EY-led workshops and complete a benchmarking analysis for the rest of the semester. After building a foundation in management consulting and learning how SCG operates, they join the ranks as consultants and take on client projects the following term. Analysts typically stay five or more semesters.

items.q: What does the EY partnership mean for me?
items.a: SCG partners with EY to train our consultants and expose us to the industry. EY holds workshops on topics useful to SCG, pairs each project with consultants and partners, and connects us to EY recruiters.

items.q: Do I have to want a career in consulting?

items.q: How much do SCG services cost?
items.a: Our on-campus client services are always free of charge. Off-campus non-profit clients are eligible for low rates designed to meet the needs of the project.
